text:
maya: Heads up — seeing a sharp spike in GPU queue times and allocation failures from eu-south about ~10m ago. Control-plane returns 503 for some schedule requests. Anyone else seeing this?
opsbot: ALERT: region-health(eu-south) degraded — scheduler-error-rate 12% | active-gpu-pools 3 -> 1 | reported by autoscaler | incident id 2029-03-12-ES
kevin: Confirmed. Traces show KV cache pressure + higher P99 latency for seq len 1024. UI shows multiple prewarm attempts failing.
liam: Is this the quota weirdness we hit last month or a real infra failure?
maya: Not quota. Backend logs have repeated "instance launch timeout" and some nodes stuck in provisioning state. Also saw NAT gateway 502s to the artifact store.
anya: Can we do a targeted traffic preference flip for latency-sensitive routes to avoid eu-south while we triage? Prefer not to fully evacuate — keep best-effort for non-critical workloads.
kevin: Agreed. Propose a soft-preference change on global router to demote eu-south to 0.2 preference for model-serving routes and keep it at 1.0 for management/control-plane traffic. That keeps admin ops still speaking to region for tear-downs.
liam: What's the exact command? Don't want to accidentally drain reserved pools or trigger scale-down.
kevin: Run this (dry-run first):
```
global-router set-preference --route-type=model-serving --region=eu-south --preference=0.2 --dry-run
# then:
global-router set-preference --route-type=model-serving --region=eu-south --preference=0.2
```
opsbot: RUN: global-router apply-change queued by kevin. Will validate health-probes for 60s post-change.
maya: I'll also toggle sticky-session TTL to 30s for impacted routes so we don't leave long-lived sessions stuck to bad backends.
kevin: Command for stickies: `global-router set-sticky-ttl --route model-serving --ttl 30s`
anya: We're preserving prewarmed pools in eu-south (reserved capacity) to avoid expensive rebuilds later, right?
liam: Checking pool-state: eu-south has 2 prewarm pools (reserved) and 1 auto pool failing launches. If we forcibly drain, we'll lose warm caches which will spike token cost later.
maya: So plan = soft-preference flip + reduce new session assignment to eu-south by ~80%, keep reserved pools warm, lower sticky-ttl. Monitor latency and error-rate for 5m. If no improvement, escalate to full failover.
kevin: I'm applying the change now. Pasting output: 
```
> global-router set-preference --route-type=model-serving --region=eu-south --preference=0.2
Applying preference change...
Scheduling weight update to edge-proxies (n=48)
Update queued, starting rolling apply
Probe checks: 50/50 healthy, 10/50 degraded -> continuing
Apply complete (started 1890123465, finished 1890123488)
```
opsbot: NOTIFICATION: preference-change complete. Auto-health-check OK.
liam: Early signals: P95 token latency from clients routed to na-central dropped ~30ms; overall model-serving error-rate down 6%. Good.
anya: Cost note — cross-region egress will increase for traffic we move out of eu-south. Estimate +8% in token network egress for the next 2h. Flagging to finance.
maya: Thanks. Also we're seeing a few control-plane 502s still for artifact fetch. I'll open a separate ticket with eng-infra-storage to check NAT / egress path.
kevin: We should also enable a short-lived circuit-breaker for deployments hitting 10% deploy-failures so they auto-fail to local fallback variants rather than keep retrying and filling the scheduler queue. I'll draft a feature request.
liam: Copy that. For now, metrics look stable. We'll hold soft-preference for 30m and then slowly nudge back if eu-south recovers.
opsbot: REMINDER: create follow-up incident ticket for RCA and cost impact, assign to eng-infra and infra-storage.
maya: On it — created INC-2029-118: "eu-south provisioning failures -> soft-pref failover". Will include logs + the weight-change diffs.
anya: Good run. Ping if we need full evacuation. :thumbsup:
kevin: One more note: when we revert, do it in small increments (0.1 steps) and watch P99 — don't flip back to 1.0 in one go.
maya: Ack. Closing thread for active ops unless something regresses.
kevin: I'll leave a comment in the incident with the command history and the probe outputs.
liam: TY everyone.
